conflicts.fact: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart / route; also direction of oxygen journey vs. L5 reading is consistent, but cumulative model contents are mislabelled across lessons
conflicts.versions: L5 states oxygen goes via pulmonary veins to left heart (consistent); L6 lists the cumulative model as L2 = gas exchange pathway, L3 = ventilation mechanism, L4 = alveolus cross-section, L5 = circulatory, whereas actual L2 = respiratory surface comparison, L3 = structure/adaptations, L4 = breathing mechanics (L5 = circulation).

conflicts.fact: Which lesson the cumulative model was begun in
conflicts.versions: L1 has learners draw the first naive model in Lesson 1; L10 says the cumulative model has been built 'since Lesson 2'; L9 says cellular respiration diagram first drawn in L6 (fine).

conflicts.fact: Cause of the burning sensation in leg muscles
conflicts.versions: L7, L10, L12 and L11 explain the burning as lactic acid from anaerobic respiration due to insufficient oxygen; L8 explains it as a shift in fuel from carbohydrate to fat (lower RQ) demanding more oxygen, and says the shift to fat occurs during prolonged exercise, whereas intense exercise relies more on carbohydrate.

conflicts.fact: Lesson in which the thoracic cavity diagram was begun
conflicts.versions: L4 says learners retrieve the labelled thoracic cavity diagram begun/annotated in Lesson 3, but L3 covers respiratory surfaces (alveoli, gills, tracheae) with no thoracic cavity diagram.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson answers 'where oxygen goes' and sequence of explanation in cumulative model
conflicts.versions: L3 ends with oxygen → alveolus → blood → (next question) → muscle cell, and L6 summary of model layers shifts lesson numbering for gas exchange/ventilation/alveolus compared with the actual lesson order.
L3 says about 700 million alveoli; L10 says ~70 m² alveolar surface area (consistent); L2 describes alveolus only qualitatively. No direct conflict.

conflicts.fact: Explanation of burning sensation and warmth; DQB question assignments
conflicts.versions: L9 explains muscle burning/warmth through enzyme-controlled metabolic heat; L10 attributes burning to lactic acid from anaerobic respiration at low oxygen.

conflicts.fact: What stimulates faster breathing / explanation of breathing rate
conflicts.versions: L6 says breathing rate rises because muscle cells need more oxygen delivered for ATP; L12 says increased CO₂ and decreased O₂ in blood stimulate breathing; L6 says question 'Why does breathing rate increase' fully explained at L6 while L7/L12 continue to develop it.

conflicts.fact: Pulse values for the anchoring data and who recorded them
conflicts.versions: L1 example 72 → 120+ bpm; L5 cites Amina 74 → 128; L6 Achieng 74 → 128 with breathing 16 → 34; L4 cites Wanjiku 14 → 28 and Baraka 16 → 30; L12 says pulse 'doubled' in L11 while data shows ~1.7x rise; L8 and L11 say pulse 'doubled' vs. L1 'rose sharply (72 → 120+)'.
